Alexa further recalled how Carlos, 37, had “just stopped it” without the duo even discussing his viewing habits.

“I’m so thankful, so grateful I was able to just stop,” Carlos said, noting he’s since refrained from starting again during marital dry spells. “When our intimacy wasn’t great, I have so much respect for our marriage that, like, I don’t want to disappoint you. For me, I know you would stay with me … [but] I just want to make sure that I honor you and I respect how much you live because if I lose that, I almost feel like I’m losing something I can’t ever get back.”

He continued, “We have something so pure right now, that one mistake will taint it . We’re human, I don’t think you can fully earn that trust back. I think you can gain a level of it, but to get that full transparency and trust? No way. So, to me, I’ve put that at such a high level that it’s not worth it at all.”

items.title: Man Sentenced for Beating Paralyzed Veteran to Death With Wooden Log in 2008
items.summary:
A California man convicted of beating a paralyzed military veteran to death with a wooden log has been sentenced to prison in a case that was solved after nearly two decades.

Jeffrey Roberson was sentenced on Monday, November 16, to 26 years to life in prison in the 2008 killing of Cecil Zachary Jr. at Zachary’s Oceanside home, according to the San Diego County District Attorney’s Office .

“This was a brutal and intentional killing of a vulnerable victim in his own home,” San Diego County District Attorney Summer Stephan said in a news release. “For more than 18 years, Cecil’s loved ones endured the pain and unanswered questions surrounding his death.”

A jury found Roberson, 60, guilty of first-degree murder on August 27 following a six-day trial, with the special allegation that he used a wooden log to kill Zachary, who was 51 when he died, according to prosecutors.

Suspected Killer Arrested in 1994 Cold Case Stabbing of Man in San Diego 

A home care nurse found Zachary dead in his hospital bed, with a towel covering his face, in his living room on June 19, 2008, prosecutors said.

Officers called to Zachary’s house located a wooden log inside the residence, believing it was used as the murder weapon.

Zachary was paralyzed below his waist after he was injured in a car crash several years prior to his death, and often remained in his hospital bed, prosecutors said.

His cause of death was “blunt-force injuries to the head,” the county’s medical examiner determined, according to the district attorney’s office.

items.title: Bowen Yang 'Genuinely' Apologizes for Making Antisemitic Comment on Podcast
items.summary:
Bowen Yang has broken his silence after making an antisemitic comment on a recent episode of his “Las Culturistas” podcast .

“I want to genuinely apologize for using a word on the podcast without knowing its antisemitic history, especially since we’ve repudiated antisemitism on the show as recently as the last two weeks,” Yang, 36, wrote in a Friday, November 20, Instagram statement.

Yang used an antisemitic slur to refer to singer Regina Spektor on an October podcast episode, which has since sparked backlash. 

“Particularly upsetting to realize that I adopted language popularized by the far-right movements whose rhetoric we should be wary of and act against,” Yang added in his statement.

Did Bowen Yang Distance Himself From Dave Chappelle on ‘SNL’? 

After uploading the statement to his Instagram Stories, the comedian added a follow-up slide with the caption, “At the same time, Free Palestine.”

During his podcast episode last month, guest Edy Modica  claimed Spektor, 46, was “a little Israel hardcore.” In response, Yang said, “Yeah, she’s Zio.” (The term is widely considered to be a slur popularized by former Ku Klux Klan leader David Duke .)

Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images for Tony Awards Productions
